what: A9-desktop: the operator draws the book box, on the computer rather than the phone (owner's call). tools/book_box_editor writes <page_dir>/book_box.json; pipeline/book_boundary.user_box pads it; Stage 02 checks its provenance and cuts the padded box.
why_this_and_not_more_detection: docs/data/a10_background_first_20260828.json: eight families of cue measured, none separates 'the book fills the frame' from 'the mask merged the book with the room'. A9 is the option the plan ranks as having a guaranteed ceiling, and Phase 1 made the detector's 'I did not find the book' honest, which is the moment to ask a human.

acceptance.split_eval: 19/21, exit 1, worst clipping 0.0% - unchanged, no book_box.json in testset/
acceptance.test_suite: 569 passed (was 554; +15 for the operator box and the editor)
acceptance.absent_case: no book_box.json => book_crop_source 'detector' and byte-identical behaviour, asserted in tests

does_it_work.method: Feed the eight hand-read boxes in gt/book_box.json as if an operator had drawn them. Those were read with ruler overlays off the committed pixels, which is what a careful drag approximates.
does_it_work.result: 8 of 8 spreads split correctly, INCLUDING both frames that fail today

why_the_drawn_box_is_padded_not_used_as_.question: gt/book_box.json fed in straight makes 'clips 0.00%' true by construction. What does a real DRAG produce? A 4080px frame shown ~1000px wide is ~4 image px per screen px.

emit_equals_drawn_box_exactly.verdict: loses text on any realistic drag

emit_equals_drawn_box_padded_by_search_p.verdict: SHIPPED - and it is what find_book's own _union(emit, search) produces anyway

symmetric_error.clipping: 0.00% at every step measured, both directions

one_sided_error_is_the_dangerous_one.found_how: By driving the tool in a browser and making the mistake: a drag ~400px too wide on the RIGHT only took paleset_01's ink ratio from 0.44 to 0.56 and lost the split entirely. The perturbation sweep had only tested SYMMETRIC error.
one_sided_error_is_the_dangerous_one.mechanism: the spine is searched in the middle 30-70% OF THE DRAWN BOX, so extra width on one side slides the book sideways inside it until the spine leaves the band
one_sided_error_is_the_dangerous_one.what_shipped_because_of_it: the editor now SHADES the 30-70% band of the drawn box and draws the last gutter it found, so an off-centre box is visible rather than a surprise; and the header hint says extra room on one side is the mistake, not sloppiness in general

safety_rules_that_ship: the drawn box is padded outward by search_pad before anything is cut

a box whose frame or frame_size does not match the current anchor is REFUSED with a stated reason, and the detector runs instead - a box drawn on a re-run anchor is a wrong crop carrying a human's confidence
a degenerate or sub-min_area_frac box is refused in the editor BEFORE it is written, and again in Stage 02
a corrupt book_box.json is treated as absent, never as an error - the convenience tool must not be able to stop a page processing
deleting the file restores the detector byte-for-byte
book_crop_source records detector | operator | operator-refused, because 'applied False' alone cannot distinguish a refused operator box from a page nobody drew on
